title: Fire
alt: A section along a row of racks in the data hall. Along the ceiling run an air-sampling pipe with small holes and a grey dry sprinkler pipe with heads. A server overheats: an orange and red hot spot appears in one rack and grey smoke rises. The sampling holes pull in a little air and the detector on the wall sounds an alarm, a flashing red light. The sprinkler pipe turns light blue as it fills with water. Only the head over the fire opens, and light-blue water sprays onto that rack. A red 2 h fire-rated wall closes the room.
sources: Dual-interlock pre-action system: Cologix VAN1 and VAN4 specification sheets 2026 (operator claims)
Design basis: NFPA 75 (2024) Fire Protection of Information Technology Equipment, 6.1.1 and 6.1.3 (clause numbers only)

steps.caption: Along the ceiling of the data hall run two pipes: an air-sampling pipe that keeps drawing in air to check it for smoke, and a sprinkler pipe that is kept dry.
A server overheats, and smoke starts to rise from its rack.
The air-sampling pipe draws the smoke to a detector, which sounds the alarm.
Only now does the sprinkler pipe fill with water. Until a fire is found it stays dry, so a leak can’t drip onto the servers.
Only the head over the fire opens, and it sprays that rack alone.
Sites in Vancouver describe this as a dual-interlock pre-action system: it needs both a detected fire and an open head before water flows.
